Something I wonder is why does the west coast not have as much development? In the past ten years, California has been developing and growing like crazy. In addition, Seattle itself is growing and becoming a secondary hub for the tech industry.

|---|---|---|

Where and Why?" by Elizabeth of Iowa and “Everyone's Headed East: Land Development Shows an Increase in the East and Barely Any in the West.” By Kerry of Chicago and "Spreading Out: New Land Development in the US" by Kaitlin of Massachusetts.

raw_comment:
Sprawling across America: The increasing size of our cities
We notice that new land has developed a lot where there are big cities and a large population. Also, the east coast tends to have more development than the rest of the country. The midwest has the least amount of development. Oregon looks like it has the least amount of development. Although Connecticut is small it does look like it has the most development. Texas development is very condensed in some areas but in the rest very condensed. Most states have either very condensed areas only in certain spots or are not very condensed but have small spots all over. We wonder how much more previously natural we have destroyed before 2008. I wonder why there is more land development in smaller states rather than larger ones. This impacts us in many ways, for example, since this map shows how urban sprawl is leading to increasingly large metropolitan areas, this could negatively impact our community by getting rid of wildlife areas and replacing them with man-made structures.

raw_comment: In the data provided by the graph, our group found several things that caught our interest. First, we noticed much of the new development has taken place around major cities. While the urban areas in cities remain the same, developments are created in suburban areas surrounding the cities. A lot of new developments have occurred in some of the most populated states, such as Texas, California, and Florida. We also noticed that many of the new developments are concentrated in one specific area rather than being spread throughout a state. In Minnesota, the development was centered around the Twin Cities - we wonder if most of the development in other states are around major cities as well? Additionally, what is going around in the western area of North Dakota and why is so much development taking place there? We also found that there was not a lot of recent development in Maine? Are property taxes too high? What would cause private or public contractors to build elsewhere? Based on these new developments, this impacts both us and our community as new development is important for creating opportunities and providing for an expanding population. As development continues across the country, it is important that investments are made in states where new infrastructure is direly needed. We would title this headline, “As the U.S. Population Expands, so do the Nation’s Cities.”

raw_comment: This graph shows the amount of new land development across the continental United States. Based on the graph, our group noticed that there seems to be a fair bit more development on the eastern side of the United States. Title: Which states are developing the fastest? 
We notice that a lot of new land development happens around big cities. There is a large area of the east coast that has a lot of new land development. We also notice that the land development areas tend to be really condensed in one area. One state with lots of land development is Texas.
We wonder why the east seems to have more new land development vs the west and why are some of the newer land developments even necessary…? Also, we wonder if maybe there might be a relation between the number of people who develop new land and the population of people in the United States? The impact that we are seeing is that many suburbs are being developed right now. There are a lot of rings on this map, and that shows that inner city land is not being developed right now. Instead, there is a ton of work being done in the suburbs. Expanding metropolitan areas are very common right now as shown in this graph.

raw_comment: I notice that this is a map which tells us where new land has developed in the continental Untied States in the past decade. The blotches of red are areas where land was developed for homes, commercial centers, large buildings, and other facilities. I also notice that there is less land development in the west while there is more in the east. I wonder as to why is it that we see more land development in the east and not the west. This is because the west is notorious for having so much space and less developed land, so I would like to know why there is more development in the east if this area is already pretty condensed and immensely developed. This impacts my community in the sense that I live in the Northeast, and I worry that there will be too much development in my area. With land development comes more people, so it makes me a little anxious that my community may become very overpopulated. I know that in California, specifically L.A, there already is a lot of people there and the air quality is not  so healthy. Hopefully the same does not happen here. Potential catchy headline: "How Does Land Development Impact Your Future?"
